sourceInventory.title: Mushrooms: Not Just for Pizza Anymore!

image1.title: Mushrooms: Not Just for Pizza Anymore!
image1.intro: You might know mushrooms as the squishy things on top of pizza. But did you know they’re not plants — and they can be used to make furniture, clothes, and even building bricks? Mushrooms are part of a whole hidden world under our feet and we’re just starting to discover how powerful they really are!
image1.heading: What Are Mushrooms Made Of?
blocks: Mushrooms are fungi, not plants and not animals!

They grow from a hidden network of tiny threads underground called mycelium (say: my-SEE-lee-um). Mycelium acts like the roots of the mushroom and spreads through soil, trees, and even dead plants to find food.
Mushrooms are made of: mycelium (the base and root system), water (up to 90%!), proteins and fiber, chitin (a tough material also found in insect shells)
Unlike plants, mushrooms don’t need sunlight. They grow in dark, damp places and “eat” nutrients from other things, like wood or compost.
visualLabels: fruit body begins to form from mycelium
Did You Know? Mycelium can heal itself if damaged like a living sponge.

image2.heading: What Are the Benefits of Mushrooms?
blocks: Mushrooms are packed with good stuff that helps your body stay strong. Many mushrooms are rich in vitamins like B and D, which help with energy and strong bones.

They also have antioxidants, which protect your cells and help your immune system fight off sickness. Some types, like shiitake and maitake, are even used in medicine to help people feel better and stay healthy.

image3.heading: What Can You Make Out of Mushrooms?
subheadings: Mushroom Furniture by Danielle Trofe (MushLume Lamps)
blocks: Artist Danielle Trofe makes lights and lamps out of mushroom materials, called MushLumes. She mixes corn stalks and hemp with live mycelium, then presses the mix into a mold shaped like lamp parts. After a few days, the mycelium grows and glues the shape together; once it’s dried and “baked,” it becomes a light, soft, and sturdy lampshade—eco-friendly and compostable.

A company called Ecovative Design creates packaging that looks like Styrofoam but is made from mycelium and agricultural waste. They pack this mix into molds (like clamshells or wine bottle holders) and let the mycelium grow until it turns into a solid shape. It’s strong, safe, and composts into soil in just a few weeks—no pollution!
image3.funFact: ⚡ Fun Fact! The largest living thing on Earth is a giant mycelium mat in Oregon. It’s over 2,000 acres wide!
